children: stock dipped 2.4% in Wednesday after-hours trading after the homebuilder reduced its full-year guidance as challenging conditions continue to dog the housing market.
Mortgage rates rose to 6.8% at the end of its fiscal Q3, and consumer confidence has declined as inflation remains above the Fed's 2% target.

params.linkText: trimmed its guidance for FY 2026 deliveries

children: to 80,000-81,000 from its prior guidance of ~82,000-83,000 homes and compared with the S&P CapIQ consensus of 82,318.

"By maintaining volume, we have improved execution across numerous key metrics," said Lennar Executive Chairman, CEO, and President Stuart Miller. "Our construction cost per square foot improved another 1% sequentially, 6% year-over-year, and 14% since our fourth quarter 2023 baseline."

The homebuilder expects Q4 new orders of 19,500-20,500 vs. the Visible Alpha consensus of 20,039. Deliveries for the quarter are projected to be 22,000-23,000, less than the 24,040 consensus. The average sales price is expected to be $370K-$380K vs. the Visible Alpha estimate of $383K.
Fiscal Q3 GAAP EPS of $1.19, trailing the average analyst estimate of $1.29, fell from $2.29 in last year's Q3.
Revenue for the quarter ended Aug. 31, 2026, decreased % to $8.05B, missing the consensus estimate of $8.37B.
Q3 new orders fell 9% Y/Y to 20,879, missing the Visible Alpha consensus of 21,424.
Deliveries in the quarter were 20,840, down 3% Y/Y.
